full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique CJ. This civil appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 13.02.2013 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.101 of 2006 reversing those dated 15.02.2006 passed by the Joint District Judge, Third Court, Tangail In Other Class Suit No. 10 of 2002. 

 6. After hearing the parties and considering the evidence and materials on record, the Joint District Judge, Third Court, Tangail, by the judgment and decree dated 15.02.2006 decreed the suit. Against the said judgment and decree, the defendant No.1 preferred First Appeal No.101 of 2001 in the High Court Division which was allowed. Thus, the plaintiff has preferred this appeal upon getting leave. 

 7. Mr. Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that the School Committee sent the order of dismissal to the Appeal and Arbitration Committee of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dhaka for necessary approval which was not approved and the Board directed the school authority to settle the dispute amicably but the headmaster-in-charge delayed to settle the dispute amicably. In such circumstances, the plaintiff approached the Board and the Board directed the school authority to allow the plaintiff to perform the duties and functions of headmaster of the School but, unfortunately, two days thereafter, the Board the passed impugned order staying its earlier decision to join the School, the High Court Division erred in law in not declaring the last order of the Board is illegal. He further submits that the letter issued by the Inspector of Schools on 18.06.2002 staying operation of letter dated 21.04.2002 though pursuant to the said letter the appellant had been working as Headmaster of the School, the High Court Division erred in law in set-ting the judgment and decree of the trial Court thereby unsited the appellant from the post of Headmaster of the school. 

 8. Mr. A.B.M. Siddiqur Rahman Khan, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.2, submits that pursuant to the order dated 21.04.2002 the appellant did not take over the charge of the headmaster of the School. He was convicted and sentenced so question of taking over charge does not arise, the High Court Division rightly reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 11. Mr. A.B.M. Siddiqur Rahman Khan, appearing for the contesting respondent, submits that appellant Rafiqul Islam was found guilty under section 406 of the Penal Code and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of 5 (five) years and to pay a fine of Tk.10,000/-, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of 2(two) years more by the Magistrate, First Class, Tangail in C. R. Case No.234 (1)1999 on the charge of giving appointments of some persons receiving Tk. 1,57,000/-. His conviction and sentence was affirmed by the Additional Sessions, Court No.1, Tangail in Criminal Appeal No.36 of 2003 by the judgment and order dated 08.02.2009. Against which, the appellant filed Criminal Revision No.282 of 2006 in the High Court Division. The High Court Division, by the judgment and order dated 14.03.2013, made the Rule absolute acquitting the appellant on the charge brought against him. He submits that though the appellant claimed that he had been performing the duties as Headmaster of the School but about 10(ten) years since 19.02.2003 to 14.03.2013 he was an accused of a criminal case. Admittedly, the appellant crossed his retiring age. On close reading of the materials produced by the School, it appears to us that the appellant did never performing his duties as Headmaster of the School after the order of dismissal. Moreover, till 2013, criminal case for misappropriation and breach of trust was pending against him. Since the appellant has crossed the date of his retirement and he did not perform any duty and function as headmaster of the school since 2003, we are of the view that the High Court Division rightly set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court.
